paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The changes in Efficacytop (the rate of successfully maximizing the object's probability) and noise_E with the number of edits. The top figure displays results for GPT2-XL using AlphaEdit and MEMIT, while the bottom figure shows results for LLaMA3-8B using only AlphaEdit. MEMIT is excluded for LLaMA3-8B due to its excessively high noise_E, making visualization difficult.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between edit count and two metrics: efficacy and noise. The x-axis is labeled “Edits”, has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 3000, and displays tick labels at 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, and 3000. The y-axis is labeled “Efficacy<sub>top</sub>” on the left and displays a linear scale from approximately 80 to 100, with tick labels every 5 units, while the right y-axis is labeled “noise<sub>E</sub>” and displays a linear scale from 0 to 5, with tick labels every 1 unit. A dashed red line representing “AlphaEdit Efficacy<sub>top</sub>” begins at approximately (0, 98) and declines to approximately (3000, 82). A solid red line representing “AlphaEdit noise<sub>E</sub>” begins at approximately (0, 1) and increases to approximately (3000, 5).
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the relationship between efficacy and noise with an increasing number of edits for the LLaMA3-8B model. The x-axis is labeled “Edits” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 3000, with tick marks at 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, and 3000. The y-axis is split into two scales; the left y-axis is labeled “Efficacytop” and has a linear scale from 80 to 100 with tick marks at 80, 85, 90, 95, and 100. The right y-axis is labeled “noiseE” and has a linear scale from 0 to 6 with tick marks at 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. A dashed red line with square markers represents “AlphaEdit Efficacytop,” starting at approximately 80 at 0 edits and decreasing to approximately 92 at 3000 edits, with values of approximately 96 at 500 edits and 93 at 1500 edits. A solid red line with circular markers represents “AlphaEdit noiseE,” beginning at approximately 1 at 0 edits and increasing to 5 at 3000 edits, with a value of approximately 3 at 2500 edits and a sharp decline to approximately 1.5 at 3000 edits.
